app.title: SWEETer-Cat
app.summary: A person browses a catalogue table of stars, one row each with measured parameters, their errors and a reference, sorted by when each row was last updated, and opens any star's own page. That page lists the star's parameters and its planets, with a strip showing where each planet's orbit sits relative to the star's habitable zone and the Solar System planets. On the plotting pages the person picks any two catalogue parameters as axes and an optional third as colour, then sets the axis limits, linear or log scales and an optional filter to keep only homogeneously derived values. The plot shows marginal histograms and a count of the objects in range. A linked page shows a two-by-two grid of scatter plots in which brushing in one panel highlights the same objects in all four, and the full table can be downloaded as TSV, CSV or HDF.

task.text: Explore a catalogue of objects and their measured parameters by looking each one up and plotting any parameter against any other, then download the table for analysis elsewhere.

data.text: A catalogue table of stars with measured parameters and their uncertainties, a reference and a homogeneity flag, joined by star name to a second catalogue of planets with orbital and physical parameters.
data.item: a star in the catalogue, with its parameters and any planets that orbit it

stage.text: exploring a compiled parameter catalogue before statistical study

mechanism.text: A sortable, searchable table of all objects links each row to a detail page. Separate plot pages turn a settings form (axes, colour column, limits, scales, homogeneous-only filter) into a zoomable scatter plot with marginal histograms that share its axes, or into a two-by-two grid of scatter plots with linked brushing.

field.text: catalogue of spectroscopic stellar parameters for exoplanet host stars in astrophysics

workflow.name: explore a catalogue by plotting any attribute against any other

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A scrolling table lists every star with its parameters, errors, reference, homogeneity flag and last-updated date, newest first. The table can be sorted and searched.

Clicking a star's name opens its page, which shows the star's general information, atmospheric parameters and mass, plus each planet's mass, radius, period, semi-major axis and equilibrium temperature.

steps.step: choose what to plot and filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Selects choose the x, y and optional colour columns, the scales, the colour and the colour scheme. Text boxes set the x and y limits, and a checkbox keeps only homogeneously derived parameters.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The plot title counts the objects that fall inside the axis limits. Marginal histograms show the distribution along each axis, with bins scaled to the number of points.
A two-by-two grid crosses two x and two y parameters, coloured by a third. Brushing points in one panel highlights the same stars in all four.
Buttons download the whole catalogue as TSV, CSV or HDF. The CSV and HDF files are converted on request and then removed from the server.

distinctive: A homogeneity flag marks parameters derived with one consistent method, and a checkbox restricts every plot to those values.
The star catalogue is joined by name to an external planet catalogue, so the plot pages can mix stellar and planetary parameters.

Each star's page draws its planets along semi-major axis, set against the inner and outer habitable-zone limits computed from the star's temperature and luminosity, with the Solar System planets shown for reference.
If a log scale is chosen for data that includes non-positive values, the axis falls back to linear and a notice says so.
Every parameter column has an error column next to it, and column headers explain their units on hover.

parts.title: Orbit and habitable-zone strip

parts.summary: Plots any catalogue parameter against any other as a zoomable scatter plot, optionally coloured by a third, with hover tooltips naming each star and a count of the objects within the limits.

parts.summary: Picks the x, y and colour columns, linear or log scales, colour and colour scheme, and axis limits, and can keep only homogeneously derived parameters.
